title: Dispatcher rollout runway and operator daily slate — Apr 2027
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact day-by-day runway and operator slate for the Dispatcher release (dispatcher v2.3.0) targeting Apr 12–14 2027. Focus: reduce blast radius for routing changes, validate smart-routing heuristics, and exercise fallback lanes to model-variant groups. This is a working checklist — expect iterative edits during dry runs.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: host routing change (policy-level), traffic-splitting heuristics, small per-route config schema update. No model weights change.
- Audience: release engineers, on-call SREs, Dispatcher service owners, console/observability leads, solutions eng for key customers.

Quick summary (what's in this release):
- Introduced policy-level soft-precedence for latency-sensitive routes (config flag: route_latency_precedence).
- New canary weighting algorithm (adaptive-decay) to progressively shift traffic based on P99 delta.
- Telemetry tags added: dispatcher.policy_v, dispatcher.canary_epoch.
- Console: per-route rollback button + audit link.

Runway calendar (high level):
- 2027-04-05 — Dry run 1: lab only, synthetic load (obs team) — smoke & KV cache behavior.
- 2027-04-08 — Dry run 2: staging with sampled production traces (10%) — measure P50/P95/P99.
- 2027-04-10 — Preflight readiness + final config pin (freeze at 17:00 PT).
- 2027-04-12 — Canary day 1: 1% traffic to canary lane, 60m observation windows.
- 2027-04-13 — Canary day 2: if green, 10% -> 25% with staggered pulses, 30m windows.
- 2027-04-14 — Ramp to 50% then to 100% over maintenance window if metrics stable.

Preflight checklist (to complete before 2027-04-10 17:00 PT):
- [ ] PRs merged: dispatcher core + console feature flag (GH #389) — confirm green builds.
- [ ] Linear blocker list cleared: RED-1427 (routing test flakiness) must be resolved or documented mitigation.
- [ ] Telemetry: new tags instrumented and verified in staging traces (obs).
- [ ] Smoke scripts updated (smoke-dispatcher.sh) and run against staging.
- [ ] Backfill: configuration backup export taken (s3://redwood-backups/dispatcher-configs/2027-04-10.json).
- [ ] Release notes draft published to release channel and to sales/CS for heads-up.
- [ ] Rollback image/build id known and pinned.
- [ ] Pager rotations assigned for Apr 12–14 (see Operator roster below).
- [ ] Canary gating thresholds finalized (see Telemetry gates).

Day-of (canary pattern + operator slate):
- Canary 0 (initial 1%): 09:00 PT deploy canary lane set, wait 10m for container warmups.
  - Operator tasks:
    - Watch: p50/p95/p99 latency by route (dashboard: Dispatcher > Canary > latencies).
    - Watch: error-rate (5xx) and client-side retries.
    - Check: KV cache hit-rate, prefix cache eviction rate (should be stable).
  - Decision after 60m: if all gates green, schedule Canary 1; else trigger rollback.

- Canary 1 (10% pulses): 11:00 PT increase to 10% in two pulses (5% -> 10%), 30m observation windows.
  - Operator tasks:
    - Validate adaptive-decay behavior: the canary should not overshoot weight beyond set thresholds.
    - Confirm console per-route rollback shows correct audit link.

- Canary 2 (25% -> 50%): 14:00 PT depending on telemetry; escalate to director call if borderline metrics.

Rollback criteria (hard stops):
- Any route experiences >3x baseline P99 increase sustained for two consecutive windows.
- Global 5xx increase >0.5% absolute over baseline for 15 minutes.
- KV cache eviction rate spike >20% relative to baseline and sustained for 10m.
- Any single high-value customer reports functional regressions (CS ticket + Slack #cs-urgent).

Soft-fallbacks (automated):
- Smart routing will auto-fallback to last-known-good policy when node-level latency crosses threshold. This is a best-effort path — still escalate to humans if triggered more than twice in one hour.

Telemetry gates (to mark a window green):
- P99 latency by route: <= baseline + 15%
- Error-rate (5xx) by route: <= baseline + 0.2% absolute
- Percent of requests hitting canary: as expected by weight +/- 2%
- No unhandled NPEs or panics in logs (search: level=error AND message~"panic" in last 30m)

Operator roster (Apr 12–14):
- Primary release engineer: Ava Rodriguez (09:00–17:00 PT)
- Secondary SRE: Marcus Li (09:00–21:00 PT)
- Observability lead: Priya Kapoor (08:00–12:00 PT)
- Console/UX on-call: Sofia Nguyen (10:00–16:00 PT)
- Escalation: Eng Director on-call (PagerDuty)

Communication plan (channels & cadence):
- Preflight announcement (Slack #release-runway) 24h before.
- Live updates in #release-runway during canaries every 30m (short bullets).
- Customer-facing status page updates if a rollback or >30m outage occurs.
- Post-release debrief in #eng-release within 24h.

Release notes (draft — for internal review):
- Title: Dispatcher v2.3.0 — policy soft-precedence + adaptive canary
- Summary: Adds route-level latency precedence policy and an adaptive canary algorithm to reduce manual tuning during rollouts. Includes console improvements for per-route rollback and additional telemetry tags that assist observability.
- Notable changes: route_latency_precedence (config), adaptive-decay canary, telemetry tags dispatcher.policy_v, dispatcher.canary_epoch, console: per-route rollback button.
- Migration notes: No schema changes to persisted payloads. Config consumers should check the route_policy section when pinning.
- Known issues: small timing drift observed in legacy traffic-shepherd when weight pulses are below 2% — rare but tracked (RED-1427).

Post-release checklist (first 24h):
- [ ] Confirm all routes stable for 6h after 100% ramp.
- [ ] Run regression prompt set (collection: dispatcher/regression-2027-04) against production sample.
- [ ] Consolidate telemetry tags and enable long-term retention for dispatcher.policy_v.
- [ ] Draft postmortem template started if any gate tripped (link: confluence:Dispatcher Postmortem Template).

Notes to self / loose ends:
- Revisit the adaptive-decay backoff curve — still too aggressive on low-QPS routes. Consider QPS floor in next patch.
- Add automated annotation to console rollback action showing last 3 windows of P99 for audit.
- Follow up with solutions eng: craft short customer-facing note about console rollback UX.
- Need final sign-off from product on messaging (Priya to chase).

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Rollback command (opskit): opskit dispatcher rollback --image=dispatcher:2027-04-05-rc1 --reason="canary-failure"
- Staging dashboards: https://observability.redwood/dispatcher/staging/canary
- Production dashboards: https://observability.redwood/dispatcher/prod/summary
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dispatcher/pull/389
- Linear: https://linear.app/RED/issue/RED-1427

End of slate — this is intentionally compact. If you're on shift, use the checkboxes above and paste short updates to #release-runway every 30m during active canaries.
